contradictions.detail: The listing shows 47,142 mi on 10/24/2026. Carfax shows 47,154 mi recorded by the same dealer (Suncoast Porsche) at service on 10/15/2026. The later figure is 12 miles lower, which is most likely a data-entry slip.
The listing text and window sticker describe 18-inch alloy wheels with colored Porsche crest caps. The photos show aftermarket bronze wheels with a non-Porsche center cap.

critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope is provided. On a 2008 3.4L M97, this is the single most valuable test for bore scoring.
No IMS retrofit entry appears in the Carfax and no invoice is provided. A 2008 engine should carry the larger, non-serviceable bearing, but the engine number has not been provided to confirm this.
Carfax shows oil changes on 01/2026 and 10/15/2026 by Suncoast, but there is no filter-cut photo.
There is no fault-memory or cam-deviation printout. A 05/2025 Porsche Melbourne entry says 'computer(s) checked' with no detail.
The listing mentions one video, but it is not examined here. There are no drain or footwell photos. The top appears raised and intact in the photos.
There is no reported water pump, thermostat, expansion tank or radiator/condenser entry in the Carfax across 18 years.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: VIN, window sticker, itemized price and fees, and a Carfax with 25 dealer service records. However, there are no invoices. There are no repair records for two accidents, including a disabling one. No at-risk item (IMS, cooling, AOS, top) is documented.

condition.rationale: The disabling right-side accident in 2011 has no repair evidence. The photos show a visibly worn and darkened steering-wheel rim with surface cracking, and aftermarket wheels. In its favor, recent oil, plugs and brake fluid are logged and the mileage is low. Nothing proves the engine bores, cooling system or structure are sound.

price_value.rationale: $31,800 plus $1,023 in fees sits at or above the $30,807 fair-value midpoint. That is despite two reported accidents (one disabling), no IMS or cooling documentation, and aftermarket wheels. A comparable active 45k-mile 2008 S in Costa Mesa, CA asks $29,870.

mission_fit.rationale: The manual and mid-engine layout satisfy the enthusiast brief. But this is a 987.1 with M97 bore-scoring exposure, which the profile frames as a keeper-type car rather than a bridge. The asking price is far above the $10,000–$19,000 ideal band, and the accident history weighs on resale within 6–24 months.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Sarasota, FL, about 2,377 miles away. PPI access is unconfirmed, though Sarasota/Tampa has Porsche independents. CA smog and registration feasibility is not yet established. The dealer offers shipping.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: This is a Boxster S manual in Midnight Blue over Sand Beige with bi-xenons, Bose and heated memory seats. It lacks PASM, Sport Chrono and sport seats. The factory wheels have been replaced with aftermarket bronze wheels, which detracts from originality.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders for scoring (M97 3.4L), and cut the oil filter
Collision check of the right side (2011 disabling damage) and left front: paint meter, weld seams, frame/suspension mounting points, alignment specs
Durametric scan: fault memory, cam deviation, over-rev ranges, airbag/occupancy and body-electrical faults
Cooling system: expansion tank crust, water pump weep, front radiators and condensers for debris and corrosion
RMS and AOS: check the bellhousing for oil and look for startup smoke
Clutch engagement point, DMF judder and shifter feel
Convertible top cycling, cables and drive blocks, hydraulic leaks, drains and footwell dampness
Aftermarket wheel fitment (offset, hub centring, TPMS function) and tire date codes
Front control arms, coffin-arm bushings and top mounts
what_would_change_verdict: Accident repair invoices from a reputable shop plus a clean collision-specialist PPI would neutralise the largest observed issue
A clean borescope and filter cut with normal cam deviation values would substantially derisk the M97 engine
A meaningful price reduction reflecting the accident history and missing age-related service would improve value
Scoring or debris in the borescope, frame or structural repair evidence, or unresolved electrical faults from 2025 would move it decisively down
evidence.mission_note: A manual Boxster S fits the enthusiast point of view. As a 987.1 with M97 risk, priced far above the ideal bridge band and carrying a disabling-accident history, it does not fit cleanly as a low-risk 6–24 month bridge.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax and window sticker establish identity firmly: a 2008 Boxster S, 6-speed manual, Midnight Blue/Sand Beige, about 47k miles, with no DMV title brands and franchise-dealer service records. The same Carfax establishes two reported accidents, including a 2011 right-side collision with disabling damage and a tow, for which no repair documentation is provided. The history shows four owners, an 08/2024 auction sale, and two short Florida tenures. The second of those ended shortly after Porsche-dealer computer and body-electrical diagnostics in 05/2025. Photos show a worn, cracked steering-wheel rim and aftermarket wheels replacing the factory set described in the listing. None of the model-critical evidence is present: no borescope, IMS/engine-number proof, scan data, top video or cooling-system receipts. The Carfax shows no reported cooling-system work in 18 years. Asking price plus fees sits at or above the fair-value midpoint despite these open items.
evidence.next_action: Email Suncoast Porsche requesting the 2011/2016 accident repair records, the engine number, their 2026 repair orders and inspection checklist, and written confirmation that an independent Porsche-specialist PPI with borescope can be done before any deposit.
